title: D$^2$O: A Dual Debiasing Operator for Training-Free Test-Time Adaptation of Vision–Language Models
claim: Prior adaptation paradigms rely on prompt tuning or a cache alone; ours adds a plug-in debiasing operator for bias correction.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, dashed dividers, highlighted dashed module in final panel
description: Three side-by-side pipeline diagrams separated by dashed vertical lines, each sharing the same input: an animal and car image grid, a Class label, and a prompt. Panel (a) shows test-time prompt tuning. A learnable prompt feeds a frozen text encoder, the image encoder uses augmentation, CLIP predictions are selected, and a dashed backpropagation arrow loops back to the prompt. Panel (b) shows cache-based training-free TTA. Image and text encoders produce a prediction, a Keys/Values cache is queried, and the two are summed into an adapted prediction. Panel (c) is D²O (ours). It adds a blue Inference-time Debiasing Operator in a dashed teal rounded box, with orange Bias Correction and purple cache blocks, merged at a sum node. Pastel bar charts mark predictions, and snowflake icons mark frozen encoders.

abstract: Training-free test-time adaptation (TTA) for vision-language models (VLMs) can improve zero-shot classification under mild shifts, but often degrades under severe style/environment variation. We identify two shared failure modes in training-free pipelines: (i) retrieval confounding, where feature similarity is dominated by nuisance/style variation and corrupts retrieval evidence; and (ii) environment-biased priors, where VLM logits exhibit environment-dependent centered shifts that distort gating and prior-like terms. Therefore, we propose D$^2$O, a training-free debiasing operator that outputs three inference-time objects: a retrieval-oriented content feature for semantic matching, a style-aware routing coordinate for bias tracking, and debiased logits for corrected priors. D$^2$O composes plug-and-play with retrieval-based and closed-form Gaussian adapters in online and transductive settings. We further provide operator-to-decision guarantees: finite-difference covariance recovers a nuisance-sensitive subspace, routing-based EMA controls centered-logit bias estimates, and these errors yield bounded posterior log-odds perturbations, leading to a margin-based condition for label invariance. Extensive experiments show that D$^2$O achieves its clearest gains under style/environment-dominant shifts, with broader gains elsewhere. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/MAiTL-Group/D2O}.
